newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico economy still weak due to high debt - IMEF.
newsitem.headline: Mexico economy still weak due to high debt - IMEF.

text.p: Mexico's economy is still weak more than two years after the peso devaluation because credit is scarce and debt levels are high, the Mexican Association of Finance Executives (IMEF) said on Monday.

IMEF said in a statement that Mexico's economic policy had stabilised the economy and made it less vulnerable to external shocks, but said the government needed to deepen economic reforms to help the economy grow.

"The level of debt that economic agents continue to maintain and the lack of credit in the economy constitute a barrier to the recovery of the domestic market, which is still depressed," the group said.
"Besides, the economic recovery has not been even and the differences among sectors is deepening," it said.

"It is necessary to accelerate structural reform in the economy, continue with privatisations,...elaborate a tax scheme that promotes investment and give stronger support to the export sector, so that industry can create jobs and sustained long-term growth," it added.
It defended the central bank's monetary policy and said a steady peso showed there was not an excess of liquidity in the monetary system.
